A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same LogiDynamics study and contain 21 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable assessment of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations on analogical reasoning and in-context learning, plus inference-scaling experiments. Results appear in Figures 2–4, Tables 2–4, and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark and inference-scaling results, including detailed model scores in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The direct-induction, automated-inference, and abduction-plus-deduction pipelines are unchanged. Hypothesis selection, verification, refinement, and the Appendix D prompts also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate E-KAR, VASR, RAVEN, List Function, and SALT under the same modality, difficulty, and task-format coverage. The added List Function citation introduces no new evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: The compared inference pipelines and model membership remain identical in the corresponding experiments, including the reasoning-model comparisons in Table 4. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Dataset counts, difficulty thresholds, accuracy metrics, model configurations, and sampling/iteration settings are unchanged. Appendix A retains temperatures of zero for main experiments and 0.4 for hypothesis sampling.

E4.justification: Figure 4 retains the same hypothesis-selection sweep, verification/refinement analysis, and combined token-scaling analysis. No robustness tests, ablations, error analyses, or case studies are added or removed.

E5.justification: The plotted error bars and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4, main result tables, and Appendix E Tables 7–15 retain identical results. For example, Table 4 reports Deepseek-V3 accuracy of 57.2% and 69.6% with high System 2 scaling in both versions.

T1.justification: The analogical-reasoning formulation in Section 2.1 and explicit input-output task definition in Section 5 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about modality, difficulty, task-format dependence, generalization to in-context learning, and System 2 scaling. The resource statement does not change the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Explanations for System 2's free-text-generation weaknesses and hypothesis-selection/refinement saturation are unchanged. The limitations discussion still restricts the exploration to static LLMs and proposes adaptive reasoning through future tuning.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-resource repository link to the abstract; v1 provides no corresponding access pointer. Implementation settings, difficulty annotation, SALT construction, and prompts in Appendices A–D remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Li et al. (2025) to the List Function citation. Section 7.1 adds Zheng et al. (2025) for complex-logic deductive reasoning while retaining Saparov et al. (2023) for longer proofs. Both new works receive bibliography entries.

P1.justification: v2 adds the resource sentence and makes limited wording revisions to the List Function description and the deductive/inductive related-work paragraph. Section order, narrative organization, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract's spacing and line wrapping change, reflowing the opening introduction; added references also reflow the bibliography. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–15 retain their graphics, captions, structures, and placement.

improvement.justification: The new resource-access pointer and more specific literature attribution modestly improve usability and scholarly documentation. The methods, results, and appendices remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited to documentation; repository completeness cannot be assessed from the PDFs.
